findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and ignores the feature flag
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions always returns false: if the flag is enabled, the !flag expression yields false so the if is skipped and it returns false; if the flag is disabled, the if is entered and it also returns false. The feature flag FlagSqlExpressions therefore has no effect, and SQL expressions are rejected even for operators who explicitly enable the flag. The enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(...) computation plus the branch is dead code, and the function name and flag read imply the flag is supposed to control availability. If the flag is intended to keep an opt-in path (the PR description says the flag still exists), the final statement should return true; otherwise it should simply return false and drop the flag read so it is not mistaken for a working security control. As written it is a latent trap: restoring the DB implementation later would still leave the feature permanently disabled.

findings.title: Behavior change disabling SQL expressions is untested; existing SQL tests likely break
findings.body: The change makes TablesList, NewSQLCommand, SQLCommand.Execute and the QueryTypeSQL branch of ReadQuery always fail, but no test files are included in the diff. The new pkg/expr/sql/db.go stubs return errors from RunCommands/QueryFramesInto, so existing tests that call TablesList/NewSQLCommand (for example pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go and pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go) or that exercise the SQL branch of ReadQuery will now fail with 'not implemented'. There is also no new regression test asserting that a SQL expression is rejected. Add or update tests for the reader rejecting QueryTypeSQL and for the stub behavior so the security fix is covered and CI stays green.

findings.title: Misleading error message: 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'
findings.body: When SQL is disabled the reader returns fmt.Errorf('sqlExpressions is not implemented'). The feature is not unimplemented - it is deliberately disabled for security - so this user-facing error is misleading. Likewise the new stubs in pkg/expr/sql/db.go make TablesList fail, and NewSQLCommand maps that failure to 'error reading SQL command', hiding the real reason a query is rejected. Use a message that states SQL expressions are disabled/unsupported.
